MastersSupply Chain Management
M-SCM
Master's Cycle — LMD

Supply Chain Management

Orchestrate flows from procurement to delivery in a West African environment undergoing full integration.

Duration

2 years (4 semesters)

Structure

4 semesters — 120 credits

Entry requirement

Bachelor's degree required (Bac+3)

About this Master's programme

This Master's programme trains global supply chain managers capable of steering physical and information flows, from procurement at suppliers through to final delivery to the customer. The programme covers purchasing and supplier management, logistics and international transport, operations planning (S&OP, demand forecasting) as well as inventory and warehouse management.

A regional specialisation sets this track apart: port and customs logistics in West Africa, the opportunities opened up by the AfCFTA and the mastery of logistics information systems (WMS, TMS, ERP). Lean continuous improvement methods complete the graduates' toolkit, preparing them for roles as supply chain managers, logistics directors, international buyers or SCM consultants.

At a glance

Track code: M-SCM

Degree: Master — 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 credits (LMD framework)

Location: Bamako — Hamdallaye ACI 2000

Modules: 9 teaching units

Master's admission requirements

Learning objectives

  • Steer physical and information flows from procurement to delivery
  • Structure the purchasing function and manage supplier relationships
  • Organise multimodal international logistics and transport
  • Build demand plans and S&OP processes
  • Operate the supply chain's WMS, TMS and ERP systems
  • Apply Lean to the continuous improvement of the supply chain

1Flow and supply chain management

  • Flow typology
  • Push and pull flows
  • Upstream-downstream synchronisation
  • Measuring logistics performance

2Purchasing and supplier management

  • The purchasing process
  • Sourcing and tendering
  • Supplier negotiation
  • Supplier performance and development

3Logistics and international transport

  • Incoterms
  • Customs transit
  • Multimodal transport
  • Insurance and transport documents

4Planning and forecasting (S&OP)

  • Demand forecasting
  • Sales and operations planning (S&OP)
  • Master production schedule
  • Capacity management

5Port and customs logistics in West Africa

  • Regional logistics corridors
  • Port operations
  • Customs regimes
  • Trade facilitation

6The AfCFTA and regional opportunities

  • The AfCFTA framework
  • Regional value chains
  • Cross-border trade
  • African e-commerce logistics

7Logistics information systems

  • WMS (warehouse management)
  • TMS (transport management)
  • ERP and integration
  • Traceability and logistics data

8Inventory and warehouse management

  • Replenishment policies
  • Safety stock
  • Warehouse design
  • Inventories and reliability

9Lean and continuous improvement

  • Eliminating waste (muda)
  • Kaizen
  • Value Stream Mapping (VSM)
  • Lean supply chain

Indicative curriculum established from the programme reference framework ; the distribution of modules per semester is confirmed by the Direction for each intake.

Skills to be acquired

Design and steer a high-performing end-to-end supply chain
Run purchasing processes and negotiate with international suppliers
Organise international transport and manage customs operations
Build forecasts and facilitate an S&OP process
Configure and operate logistics information systems (WMS, TMS, ERP)
Deploy a Lean approach across logistics operations

Supply chain manager

Logistics director

International buyer

Procurement manager

SCM consultant

Transport manager

Warehouse and distribution manager

Career prospects are professional outlooks, not job guarantees.

Admission requirements

Bachelor's degree required (Bac+3)

Licence (Bachelor's degree) or a recognised equivalent degree in a relevant field.

Application file

Transcripts, CV and motivation letter reviewed by the Direction.

Entrance test

A written test covering the fundamentals of the specialisation and general knowledge.

English test

Assessment of English proficiency, a language worked on every semester.

Submitting an application does not constitute automatic admission ; the decision rests with the Direction.

Apply for the Supply Chain Management (M-SCM)

Submit your application online or contact the admissions team to confirm whether the track is open, the documents to provide and the academic calendar.
